requirements.description: Disclose information about the undertaking’s system to prevent and detect, investigate, and respond to allegations or incidents relating to corruption and bribery, including related training. This includes: (a) procedures to prevent, detect and address allegations/incidents; (b) whether investigators/investigating committee are separate from the management chain involved; (c) any process to report outcomes to the administrative, management and supervisory bodies; (d) if no such procedures exist, disclose this and any plans to adopt them; (e) how policies are communicated to relevant persons to ensure accessibility and understanding; and (f) training details: nature/scope/depth, percentage of functions-at-risk covered, and extent of training for administrative, management and supervisory bodies.

Disclose business conduct policies and how corporate culture is fostered, including specific anti-corruption/anti-bribery and incident-handling elements relevant to prevention systems: (a) mechanisms for identifying, reporting and investigating concerns (including whether internal/external stakeholders can report); (b) if no anti-corruption/anti-bribery policies consistent with the UN Convention against Corruption, disclose this and plans/timetable; (c) whistleblower protection (channels, training/information, anti-retaliation measures); (d) if no whistleblower protection policies, disclose this and plans/timetable (or state being subject to equivalent legal requirements); (e) procedures to investigate business conduct incidents (including corruption/bribery) promptly, independently and objectively; (g) training policy on business conduct (target audience, frequency, depth); and (h) functions most at risk regarding corruption and bribery.

Provide information on incidents of corruption or bribery during the reporting period, including: (a) number of convictions and amount of fines for violations of anti-corruption and anti-bribery laws; and (b) actions taken to address breaches in procedures and standards. The undertaking may also disclose: total number and nature of confirmed incidents; number of confirmed incidents leading to dismissal/discipline of own workers; number of confirmed incidents leading to termination/non-renewal of contracts with business partners; and details/outcomes of public legal cases regarding corruption or bribery brought against the undertaking and its own workers during the reporting period (including cases initiated in prior years with outcomes in the current period). Incidents involving value chain actors are included only where the undertaking or its employees are directly involved.

summary: To answer the question, ESRS G1 requires disclosures on (i) the undertaking’s anti-corruption/anti-bribery prevention and detection system, including investigation independence, reporting to governance bodies, policy communication, and training coverage (G1-3); (ii) related business conduct policies and mechanisms for reporting/investigating concerns, whistleblower protection, incident investigation procedures, training policy, and identification of functions-at-risk (G1-1); and (iii) confirmed incidents and legal outcomes during the reporting period, including convictions/fines, actions taken, and (optionally) details of confirmed incidents and public legal cases/proceedings and their outcomes (G1-4).
full_context:
Standard: ESRS G1
Title: BUSINESS CONDUCT
[objective.1] The objective of this Standard is to specify disclosure requirements which will enable users of the undertaking’s sustainability statements to understand the undertaking’s strategy and approach, processes and procedures as well as its performance in respect of business conduct.
[objective.2] This Standard focusses on the following matters, collectively referred to in this Standard as ‘business conduct or business conduct matters’: (a) business ethics and corporate culture, including anti-corruption and anti-bribery, the protection of whistleblowers, and animal welfare; (b) the management of relationships with suppliers, including payment practices, especially with regard to late payment to small and medium-sized undertakings. (c) activities and commitments of the undertaking related to exerting its political influence, including its lobbying activities;
[content[0].title] Interaction with other ESRS
[content[0].paragraphs[0].3] The content of this Standard on general disclosures as well as impact, risk and opportunity management and metrics and targets shall be read in conjunction respectively with ESRS 1 General principles and ESRS 2 General requirements.
[content[1].title] Disclosure Requirements
[content[1].subsections[0].title] ESRS 2 General disclosures
[content[1].subsections[0].paragraphs[0].4] The requirements of this section should be read in conjunction with and reported alongside the disclosures required by ESRS 2 on Governance (GOV), Strategy (SBM) and Management of impacts, risks and opportunities (IRO).
[content[1].subsections[1].title] Governance
[content[1].subsections[1].subsections[0].title] Disclosure Requirement related to ESRS 2 GOV-1 – The role of the administrative, management and supervisory bodies
[content[1].subsections[1].subsections[0].paragraphs[0].5] When disclosing information about the role of the administrative, management and supervisory bodies, the undertaking shall cover the following aspects: (a) the role of the administrative, management and supervisory bodies related to business conduct; and (b) the expertise of the administrative, management and supervisory bodies on business conduct matters.
[content[1].subsections[2].title] Impact, risk and opportunity management
[content[1].subsections[2].subsections[0].title] Disclosure Requirement related to ESRS 2 IRO-1 – Description of the processes to identify and assess material impacts, risks and opportunities
[content[1].subsections[2].subsections[0].paragraphs[0].6] When describing the process to identify material impacts, risks and opportunities in relation to business conduct matters, the undertaking shall disclose all relevant criteria used in the process, including location, activity, sector and the structure of the transaction.
[content[1].subsections[2].subsections[1].title] Disclosure Requirement G1-1– Business conduct policies and corporate culture
[content[1].subsections[2].subsections[1].paragraphs[0].7] The undertaking shall disclose its policies with respect to business conduct matters and how it fosters its corporate culture.
[content[1].subsections[2].subsections[1].paragraphs[1].8] The objective of this Disclosure Requirement is to enable an understanding of the extent to which the undertaking has policies that address the identification, assessment, management and/or remediation of its material impacts, risks and opportunities related to business conduct matters. It also aims to provide an understanding of the undertaking’s approach to corporate culture.
[content[1].subsections[2].subsections[1].paragraphs[2].9] The disclosures required under paragraph 7 shall include how the undertaking establishes, develops, promotes and evaluates its corporate culture.
[content[1].subsections[2].subsections[1].paragraphs[3].10] The disclosures in paragraph 7 shall cover the following aspects related to the undertaking’s policies on business conduct matters: (a) a description of the mechanisms for identifying, reporting and investigating concerns about unlawful behaviour or behaviour in contradiction of its code of conduct or similar internal rules; and whether it accommodates reporting from internal and/or external stakeholders; (b) where the undertaking has no policies on anti-corruption or anti-bribery consistent with the United Nations Convention against Corruption(120), it shall state this and whether it has plans to implement them and the timetable for implementation; (c) how the undertaking protects whistleblowers, including: i. details on the establishment of internal whistleblower reporting channels, including whether the undertaking provides for information and training to its own workers and information about the designation and training of staff receiving reports; and ii. measures to protect against retaliation its own workers who are whistleblowers in accordance with the applicable law transposing Directive (EU) 2019/1937 of the European Parliament and of the Council(121); (d) where the undertaking has no policies on the protection of whistle-blowers(122), it shall state this and whether it has plans to implement them and the timetable for implementation; (e) beyond the procedures to follow-up on reports by whistleblowers in accordance with the applicable law transposing Directive (EU) 2019/1937, whether the undertaking has procedures to investigate business conduct incidents, including incidents of corruption and bribery, promptly, independently and objectively; (f) where applicable, whether the undertaking has in place policies with respect to animal welfare; (g) the undertaking’s policy for training within the organisation on business conduct, including target audience, frequency and depth of coverage; and (h) the functions within the undertaking that are most at risk in respect of corruption and bribery.
